subject: Equinox Health — on‑prem readiness & networking hypotheses
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Bhatia <sbhatia@equinox-health.com>, Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@equinox-health.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Equinox Health — on‑prem readiness & networking hypotheses

Hi Samir / Tara,

Thanks for taking the time today — good first conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the high‑level pain, goals, and the hypotheses Redwood will validate with your team before a technical deep dive. I’ve attached a one‑page with the hypotheses + a rough on‑prem architecture diagram.

Key takeaways (from you):
- Primary driver: regulatory requirement to keep PHI and model inference on‑prem in an isolated environment (no persistent egress to public internet).
- Desired outcome: run inference behind a customer‑managed firewall with strict egress controls, KMS integration, and audit logs retained for 7+ years.
- Compatibility: existing infra is VMWare-based (vSphere); they are open to a small GPU pool or appliance; procurement prefers single‑vendor support for both infra and software.

Our working hypotheses (what we think will be required):
1) Air‑gap option: You’ll likely need an air‑gapped or tightly restricted VPC with approved outbound endpoints only (SAML + Redacted telemetry).
2) Network: Static egress IP or NAT gateway for callback services; optional private peering if Equinox wants a managed control plane connection (via a narrow set of ports).
3) Key management: Integration with your KMS/HSM is necessary for customer‑managed keys; Redwood must support bring‑your‑own‑keys and in‑flight encryption.
4) Data residency & logs: Long retention of audit logs and a way to export them for compliance audits.
5) Ops model: You’ll want a support SLA and optionally a small on‑site install window for the first deployment.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm (by EOD Fri) which connectivity model you prefer: (A) fully air‑gapped appliance (offline installs, manual updates) or (B) private VPC with tightly scoped outbound egress (Redwood control plane can use an approved NAT).
- If you choose (B), please share network range(s) and any proxy/NAT constraints; if (A), let us know if procurement requires an asset list.
- Schedule a 90‑minute technical deep dive with Dev (solutions engineer) and Laura (CS) — propose Wed 2/24 or Thu 2/25.

Attachments: equinox-network-hypotheses.pdf, proposed-onprem-architecture.png, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Re: Equinox Health — on‑prem readiness & networking hypotheses

Jasmine — thanks for the writeup and the diagrams. Quick clarifications: 

- Correct on regulatory driver (state + Fed HIPAA expectations) — we need to avoid any outbound model artifacts. Model weights and inference cache must remain in our environment.
- For connectivity model, procurement is leaning toward (B) private VPC with strict egress; they want the option for an isolated appliance down the line but not at initial roll‑out.
- Network specifics: we use a NAT pool and our egress goes through an inspection proxy. Any callbacks will need to be whitelisted through the proxy; we can provide IP ranges but need cert‑based mutual TLS for any persistent control channel.
- Timeline: procurement wants a commercial proposal and an initial SOW by end of March; technical review can be sooner.

We’re okay to do Wed 2/24 11:00am PT for the technical deep dive. Can Dev & Laura make it?

Samir
Samir Bhatia
CTO (interim), Equinox Health

- Certs: confirm whether mTLS will be terminated by your proxy or if we should plan for mutual TLS at the instance level.
- KMS: point of contact for KMS/HSM team and whether you use AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or an on‑prem HSM appliance.
- Compliance: any additional retention policies beyond 7 years and who will own log exports.

Subject: RE: Equinox Health — on‑prem readiness & networking hypotheses — tech prechecklist

Jasmine / Laura — prepping for Wed 2/24 11:00am PT. Draft tech pre‑checklist below that I’ll walk through with Equinox:

1) Control plane model: confirm whether they want (a) Redwood control plane out of band with only narrow egress (recommended for managed updates/telemetry) or (b) fully offline appliance with manual updates.
2) Egress & callbacks: list of outbound FQDNs/IPs needed for control callbacks; support mTLS for persistent channels; if proxy performs TLS termination, we’ll need cert exchange process.
3) KV cache & model weights: ensure model artifacts remain on customer storage; Redwood must support model launch from an NFS or object store mounted in‑cluster. Discuss read/write permissions and disk encryption.
4) KMS/HSM integration: list supported HSM vendors and whether Equinox requires HSM signing for every token.
5) Audit & logs: format (syslog/S3), retention policy, and an exporter (we can push to your S3 or you can pull via rsync in a weekly window).
6) Deployment ops: onprem installer steps, expected maintenance window, and rollback plan.

Attachments I’ll bring to the call: minimal port matrix, appliance hardware SKU guidance, and a sample SOW.

I’ll also prepare a short runbook for cert exchange and NAT whitelisting to reduce back‑and‑forth.

See you on Wed.

— Dev Patel
